exposure: Parents' perceptions and knowledge of neonatal jaundice
outcome: Infant manifestations in the first week after birth
cohort: 449 healthy infants admitted to a well-baby nursery and their parents participated in the study.
finding: Despite no significant correlation of exclusive breastfeeding with hyperbilirubinemia, parental concerns and perceptions of neonatal jaundice posed a significant barrier to breastfeeding in the first few days after birth.
mod_finding: Exclusive breastfeeding was found to be more common in infants born via vaginal delivery.
cross-section timing: During the first week after birth.
